lee_writer: Heads-up — PR #382 has a bunch of inconsistent phrasing for our API params. Some spots use "model name", others "model", and a few examples show `model_id`. Can we pick a single canonical form?
sara_docs: ugh, saw that. My vote is `model` (short, consistent with SDKs).
dan_engineering: +1 for `model`. backend expects `model` in the request payload. changing docs to match reduces confusion.
lee_writer: ok, go with `model`. I'll update the prose and examples. Two quick Qs: do we keep contractions in UI copy? e.g., "you'll" vs "you will".
alex_pm: for product-facing microcopy, prefer contractions to sound friendly. For API reference and migration guides, use full forms. So: friendly elsewhere, formal in reference.
rachel_ux: agree w/ alex. UX examples can be conversational. API request/response docs should be precise.
sara_docs: noted. I'll sweep the API reference for contractions + ambiguous terms. Can someone run a grep across the repo for the variants (`model name|model_id|model`) so we don't miss edgecases?
dan_engineering: running a quick search now: `git grep -nE "model_name|model_id|\bmodel\b"`. CI will return a ton.
ci-bot: quick report: 47 hits in docs/, 6 hits in examples/, 3 hits in sdk-snippets/ (see https://ci/reports/grep-model-2101357924).
lee_writer: thanks. I'll take docs/ and examples/. Dan — can you own sdk-snippets/?
dan_engineering: yep. I'll update inline SDK snippets where we pass `model_id` in examples. Also will push a compatibility note in migration guide (docs/migration/legacy-params.md).
sara_docs: small style rule for the guide: prefer param-case for endpoint query params in prose (e.g., `model`, `max_tokens`), but show camelCase in JS SDK snippets. Add a short note about casing so readers aren't surprised.
lee_writer: good point. I'll add: "Prose uses snake_case/param-case; client SDKs use idiomatic case (camelCase for JS, snake_case for Python)." Keeper?
alex_pm: yes. Add an explicit example showing the same request in curl, Python, and JS. That usually clears things up.
rachel_ux: for examples that show human-facing UI text, I'll flag when to use contractions. Add a tiny style note near the microcopy section.
sara_docs: PR plan: I'll open a follow-up PR that standardizes the API reference to `model` and expands the style guide bits. lee, can you update #382 with a checklist of files you touched so we can review quickly?
lee_writer: will do. checklist pasted in PR description. Also left TODO comments in a couple of generated examples that still use `model_id`.
dan_engineering: after my sdk-snippets PR, I'll run the snippet-tests (ci/snippet-runner). If anything breaks we roll back with a compatibility note.
ci-bot: snippet-runner scheduled for 2101358050.
sara_docs: timeline? trying to get this into the next docs deploy (tomorrow).
lee_writer: aiming for same. I'll push changes tonight. If anyone wants to pair on reviews in the AM ping me. :coffee:
sara_docs: thanks — will review after your push. :thumbsup:
lee_writer: one last edgecase — glossary term for "model family" vs "model". Some product teams use "model family" intentionally. Let's not collapse that. Add glossary entry clarifying: `model` = specific version to call; `model family` = grouping of related versions.
rachel_ux: added comment in docs/glossary.md to reflect that.
sara_docs: perfect. I'll include the glossary update in my sweep.
lee_writer: all right, moving this thread to action items: 1) lee: update prose/examples (docs/, examples/) 2) dan: sdk-snippets and compatibility note 3) sara: API reference sweep + glossary + style rules 4) rachel: microcopy flags. Ping here when PRs are open.
dan_engineering: noted, starting now.
ci-bot: PR check reminder: link PRs in the parent tracking issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/147.
sara_docs: added issue link to my draft PR.
lee_writer: thanks team — quick wins over churn.
